I've written a plan that moves the expense approvals for all four workers from Jordan Carter to Kofi Silva in Finance. Each worker gets their own approver change (`fin_set_approver`), and their three pending reports get rerouted. Nothing needs to change in Workday, Identity, ITSM or Legal, and nothing needs a human decision right now.

**What I found:**
- **Workday is already up to date.** All four workers (Ines Iyer, Noah Patel, Noah Alvarez and Avery Novak) show Kofi Silva as manager. The change took effect 2026-11-01 and today is 2026-11-02. No other events have arrived since these four.
- **Finance still has Jordan Carter as approver for all four.** Three reports are still waiting on him: Ines's exp-2c70501e ($599), and Avery's exp-e8147dc9 ($900) and exp-scn-C5002 ($640). Changing the approver only affects new submissions, so these three need moving separately.
- **Why not one bulk reassignment of Jordan's workers:** that would also move Kofi himself. Kofi is on Jordan's approval list and still reports to Jordan, so he would end up approving his own expenses. Kofi's own pending report stays with Jordan.
- **Nothing else changes.** A manager change doesn't affect cost center (all still CC-1000), job profile, access groups or equipment.

**Possible blocker:** Kofi is a contractor (Contingent Worker). Finance may refuse to make a contractor an expense approver. If it does, the plan asks the Finance team to fix it once, quoting the refused worker and Kofi's WID. Only the failed steps get re-run. If Finance says it's a policy rule against contractors approving, a human has to choose a different approver.

I kept one case per event so each keeps its own correlation ID for safe retries. They are still one team move from Jordan to Kofi.

All seven finance steps are finished, and I re-read every record to confirm it. Finance accepted Kofi Silva (3da95cd2167b75dfb948f82a8317cba0) as approver, so step 8 (stop and escalate) wasn't needed.

**1–5. Expense approver set to Kofi Silva:** I set each worker's approver one at a time with `fin_set_approver`, not `fin_reassign_approvals`. Re-reading each profile shows Kofi as the approver for all four:
- Ines Iyer, 3b08c6e33c7295782d6c797f8f7d9b78 (case-82f1c080)
- Noah Patel, 867e5e15bc01bfce6a27e0dfcbf87544 (case-0575665b)
- Noah Alvarez, 721dea3bf63f23d0dbe53fcafb2147df (case-94c16aad)
- Avery Novak, a44a4d468918b6824f4a353e74300513 (case-97623f40)

**2 & 6. Pending reports moved from Jordan Carter to Kofi:** All three were still Pending Approval before I moved them, and re-reading shows each is now with Kofi:
- exp-2c70501e (Ines, $599)
- exp-e8147dc9 (Avery, $900)
- exp-scn-C5002 (Avery, $640)

**7. Final check:**
- Jordan Carter (5186ee32ee8d7ee9770348a05d300cb9) now approves only Kofi.
- Kofi now approves the four workers above.
- Kofi's own approver is still Jordan, so he doesn't approve his own expenses. His one open report stays with Jordan, which is correct.

**Note:** The set-approver and reroute tools don't accept idempotency keys, so I couldn't attach the keys from the plan. To avoid duplicates, I checked each record before and after every change instead.

Nothing is left unresolved on the finance side.

I didn't take any action for step 8 (case-82f1c080), because the condition for it wasn't met.

That step only applied if Finance had refused Kofi Silva (3da95cd2167b75dfb948f82a8317cba0) as an expense approver. The Finance executor reports that Finance accepted him and that every change was checked by re-reading the records afterwards:
- **Approver set to Kofi:** Ines Iyer (3b08c6e33c7295782d6c797f8f7d9b78), Noah Patel (867e5e15bc01bfce6a27e0dfcbf87544), Noah Alvarez (721dea3bf63f23d0dbe53fcafb2147df) and Avery Novak (a44a4d468918b6824f4a353e74300513).
- **Pending reports moved from Jordan Carter (5186ee32ee8d7ee9770348a05d300cb9) to Kofi:** exp-2c70501e, exp-e8147dc9 and exp-scn-C5002.
- **No refusals,** so there was nothing for the Finance team to fix and nothing to re-run.

So I made no fix request to Finance, no polling and no escalation to a human. My tools can't read Finance records, so I'm relying on that report rather than my own check. Nothing is left unresolved for this step.
